title: Headcount Buoyancy Index and Pricing Thresholds - Feb 2027
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a compact index (Headcount Buoyancy Index, HBI) that links short-term token price movements and throughput to dynamic hiring/trial staffing decisions. Goal is to provide an actionable trigger matrix for finance + product + recruiting to execute temporary staffing quarantines, contractor surges, or pricing nudges with minimal churn.

Executive summary / headline rules:
- HBI = (30d token spend growth rate * 0.6) + (7d active-customer-change * 0.3) + (GPU-utilization-delta * 0.1). Scaled to 0-100.
- HBI < 25: Green -> aggressive hiring + growth ops enabled (no price increases).
- HBI 25-55: Yellow -> pause non-critical hiring, enable contractor bench; evaluate per-route price tilts (+5% cap on high-cost routes).
- HBI > 55: Red -> hiring freeze, deploy soft price floor on high-cost model tiers, enable Dedicated capacity throttle policies.

Assumptions used for sensitivities:
- Baseline token price (internal blended per-token cost) = $0.00035 effective after quantization gains.
- High-price shock scenario = +40% unit cost (GPU spot surge).
- Customer elasticity: for enterprise tiers we assume 0.15 elasticity; for self-serve tiers 0.45 elasticity.

Scenario table (summary):
- Conservative (HBI +10): apply contractor surge(6 weeks), move 12% safe-batch->cold-cache, add per-route cap. Estimated 12% reduction in spend growth vs baseline.
- Baseline (HBI +30): pause non-essential hires (30 headcount deferred), implement 5% price tilt on top-10% token routes. Estimated net margin neutral after 8 weeks.
- Severe (HBI +60): hiring freeze, escalate price floor by 8% on self-serve, move 60% of low-priority requests to cheaper quantized model variants, pursue Dedicated capacity rightsizing. Estimated 18-26% reduction in burn over 12 weeks.

Headcount operational playbook (quick ops checklist):
1) HBI calculated daily by finance pipeline -> Slack alert to #ops-finance when crossing thresholds.
2) Within 24h of Yellow: product to identify non-critical hires (list and expected onboarding impact), recruiting to pause external offers.
3) Within 48h of Red: freeze external hires, evaluate internal role redeployments, open contractor sourcing runway.
4) Finance to run rapid sensitivity run (token price +/- 20% and GPU cost +/- 40%) and publish update to execs within 72h.

Pricing sensitivity notes (detailed):
- For self-serve customers small price nudges (3-5%) lead to measurable drop in daily active sessions but concentrate spend on committed slabs. Use couponing to protect enterprise retention.
- Implement routing policy: route new burst traffic to cheapest compatible model first (maintain quality gating).
- Fall-back rule: if price floor triggers churn > 12% in a 14-day window, auto-revert and shift focus to capacity hedges.

Open questions / next steps:
- Validate HBI weights with past 24 months of internal telemetry (point estimate + bootstrap CI). Priya to own dataset pull.
- Define exact per-route toggle implementation in Redwood Console. Product + Console engineering required.
- Legal to review messaging for pricing changes to customers (Alexandra).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally concise — the attached sheets (tabbed) contain the numeric scenarios, per-role headcount lists, and script snippets for the HBI calculation (Python pseudocode). Add comments inline on the sheet; this doc is the decision anchor for an initial pilot Q2 2027.
